title.zh: 指数缩放贝塞尔伽马项

summary: Evaluate the dimensionless modified-Bessel harmonic term Gamma_n(x) and its neighbor-combination derivative with broadcast integer order and real or complex argument.

identity.relation: Integer cyclotron harmonic order and dimensionless argument to Bessel-Gamma term and derivative
identity.definition: Gamma_n=ive(n,x)*exp(-x+abs(Re(x))); Gamma_prime_n=[ive(n-1,x)/2+ive(n+1,x)/2-ive(n,x)]*exp(-x+abs(Re(x))). Here ive is the exponentially scaled modified Bessel I. For representable values this is exp(-x) I_n(x) and its derivative with respect to x.
identity.model: Integer-order modified-Bessel terms used in a finite Maxwellian cyclotron-harmonic sum
identity.geometry: No spatial geometry; elementwise special-function evaluation
identity.coordinates: NumPy-broadcast axes have caller-defined meaning; no physical axis is inferred
identity.boundary: Arguments and outputs must be finite and representable as complex128; orders must be exactly representable integers of magnitude at most 2^53.
assumptions: The caller has already formed dimensionless x, such as b=(k_perp*rho_c)^2 for the fluidBW dispersion relation.
The exponentially scaled Bessel backend is retained; this callable does not select a harmonic truncation.

inputs.name: n
inputs.description: Integer Bessel order; broadcasts against x.
inputs.shape: scalar or nonempty array, broadcastable with x
inputs.dtype: real numeric with exactly integral values
inputs.constraints: Finite, not boolean or complex, exactly integral after float64 conversion, and absolute value no greater than 2^53.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Dimensionless Bessel argument; broadcasts against n.
inputs.shape: scalar or nonempty array, broadcastable with n
inputs.constraints: Finite after complex128 conversion; boolean, string and empty inputs are rejected.

outputs.name: Gamma_n
outputs.shape: broadcast shape of n and x; scalar inputs yield a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable for accepted inputs.

outputs.name: Gamma_prime_n
outputs.description: Neighbor-combination derivative of Gamma_n with respect to x.
outputs.shape: broadcast shape of n and x; scalar inputs yield a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable for accepted inputs.

preconditions: n and x are finite nonempty numeric inputs that broadcast to a common shape.
The chosen argument x and integer harmonic order have the caller's intended normalization.
supported: Negative, zero and positive integer orders; x=0 and finite real or complex x.
Scalar and array evaluation with NumPy broadcasting and no input mutation.
excluded: Noninteger Bessel orders or automatic interpretation of arbitrary x as a physical wave parameter.
Harmonic truncation, Maxwellian dispersion tensor assembly and mode/root selection.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for empty, boolean, string, nonnumeric, nonbroadcastable or nonfinite inputs, complex/noninteger/unrepresentable orders, or nonfinite x.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the scaled Bessel result or derivative is nonfinite or unrepresentable; other unexpected SciPy execution errors propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: None; both outputs are returned only after all broadcast elements pass validation.

provenance.lineage_summary: Standardized as a development relation from the saved fluidBW L1 bessel_gamma_functions candidate, now archived pending first-stage re-review, using SciPy's scaled Bessel implementation. Its saved grid and digest-bound replay are finite numerical evidence, not current qualified D1 delivery or expert-approved scientific identity for every complex argument.
source_kinds: saved historical fluidBW L1 Gamman/Gammapn operator contract and implementation
saved finite source-oracle grid and digest-bound L1 comparison

example.description: Evaluate the zero-order term and derivative at the origin.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_bessel_gamma
r = evaluate_bessel_gamma(0, 0.0)
assert r['Gamma_n'] == 1 and r['Gamma_prime_n'] == -1
example.expected: Gamma_0(0)=1 and Gamma_prime_0(0)=-1, each in a zero-dimensional complex128 array.

scope: Finite-grid comparison to the modified-Bessel definition, origin identities and complex broadcast behavior.
Saved fluidBW 98-point Gamma/Gamma-prime oracle and bounded digest-bound L1 implementation replay when the L1 root is supplied.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The SciRel tests establish listed identities and failure behavior. Optional L1 replay compares a finite saved 98-point real-argument grid with stated absolute/relative tolerances; it does not establish arbitrary complex-plane source parity, a physical choice of x, or expert approval.
known_limitations: Floating-point underflow or a nonrepresentable result can bound extreme inputs; the callable raises rather than returning nonfinite outputs.
The source implementation accepted some noninteger orders implicitly; SciRel intentionally restricts n to exactly representable integers.
The first-stage fluidBW branch-coverage question, public distribution license and expert recognition remain open.
